brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 give six compartments. They're loose bins that sit in the cells under lift-off top covers, and they hold the screw, nut and standoff props.
drawer:0#0,1#cut sits on the cut face of the half base, with tweezers inside
handle:0,0,0;top is fitted to the top covers of the three cells. The configurator checks fit only, so I can't confirm how much weight it can carry.
It's a compact three-cell case with a closed lid and a top handle. Strength and load capacity depend on the print material and aren't checked by the configurator.

finish.summary: I built a closed carry case from three base cells: two full cells, each holding a removable bin split into three sections, and a north-half cell with a drawer. All three cells have top covers, which form the lid, and a carry handle is mounted on top. Every open face is capped and the joints are bolted. check_build reports no issues and the mesh-collision check is clear. The design has 36 parts, about 1.86 kg of filament and about 44 hours of printing. The configurator only checks fit and collisions, so I can't tell you how much weight the handle will hold. I dressed the bins with M3 screws, nuts and standoffs and put tweezers in the drawer. You can't see them from outside because the lid covers them.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
